ai.definition: A nuclear reactor that uses thorium as its primary fuel source, dissolved in a liquid fluoride salt, which also serves as the coolant. The design operates at low pressure and includes passive safety features.
ai.howItWorks: Thorium is bred to fissile uranium-233 inside the molten salt, which acts both as the fuel and coolant. If the reactor overheats, the fuel-salt mixture expands and drains into a separate holding tank, reducing heat output and preventing further fission reactions.
ai.problemSolved: Addresses the issue of limited availability of traditional nuclear fuels like uranium-235 while providing a safer and more efficient alternative for baseload power generation.
ai.manufacturing: Manufactured in specialized facilities with high precision to ensure safety and efficiency. Requires advanced materials handling techniques due to the use of molten salts at elevated temperatures.
ai.buildProcess: Involves designing, constructing, testing, and licensing phases. The process is complex and requires significant expertise in nuclear engineering and material science.
ai.costDrivers: High initial capital costs for specialized equipment and safety systems, ongoing operational costs related to fuel management and waste disposal, regulatory compliance expenses.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to mature further with successful trials and scaling up of production. Potential for widespread adoption if technical challenges are overcome and regulatory hurdles are addressed.
ai.regulation: Subject to stringent safety regulations and licensing processes due to the nature of nuclear technology. Requires international cooperation on standards and protocols.
ai.risks: Technical risks related to handling molten salts, potential for accidents during operation or decommissioning, geopolitical risks associated with nuclear proliferation concerns.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain given current market conditions and regulatory environment. Potential for cost savings in the long term through reduced fuel costs and improved efficiency.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected advancements in materials science to improve reactor performance and safety. Increased focus on thorium-based reactors as part of global efforts towards sustainable energy solutions.

glossary.def: A naturally occurring, slightly radioactive metallic element that can be used as a nuclear fuel.
Capable of undergoing fission when struck by a neutron.
Chemical compounds composed of fluoride ions and metal cations, used in the molten salt reactor to both cool and act as fuel.
Safety systems that operate without external power or manual intervention during an emergency scenario.

subsystems.name: Reactor core and vessel
subsystems.role: holds the molten salt fuel and graphite moderator at low pressure.

subsystems.name: Fuel salt loop
subsystems.role: circulates the thorium-bearing fluoride salt through the core and heat exchanger.

subsystems.name: Coolant and power conversion
subsystems.role: transfers heat from the fuel salt to a working fluid that drives a turbine.

subsystems.name: Off-gas and fuel processing
subsystems.role: removes fission products and bred uranium, and adds fresh thorium.

subsystems.name: Passive safety system
subsystems.role: drains the fuel salt to a safe geometry if it overheats.

buildSteps.title: Purify the salt
buildSteps.detail: Lithium-beryllium fluoride salt (LiF-BeF2) is mixed with thorium and uranium fluorides and purified to remove oxygen and moisture, which would corrode the loop.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the vessel and components
buildSteps.detail: The reactor vessel, pumps, and heat exchangers are built from corrosion-resistant nickel alloys such as Hastelloy-N, which tolerates hot fluoride salt.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the core
buildSteps.detail: Graphite moderator blocks are stacked inside the vessel, and control rods are inserted to absorb neutrons.

buildSteps.title: Install the salt loop
buildSteps.detail: Pumps, heat exchangers, and the freeze valve are connected. The entire loop is preheated because the salt is solid at room temperature.

buildSteps.title: Melt and circulate the salt
buildSteps.detail: The salt is heated until it melts, then circulated through the core to check for leaks and verify flow.

buildSteps.title: Start up with fissile feed
buildSteps.detail: A small amount of uranium-235 or uranium-233 is added to reach criticality; thorium-232 then absorbs neutrons and breeds uranium-233.

buildSteps.title: Operate and reprocess
buildSteps.detail: Fission products are continuously stripped from the salt, especially noble gases and tritium, and fresh thorium is added to keep the fuel mixture optimal.

buildSteps.title: Generate electricity
buildSteps.detail: Hot fuel salt heats a secondary salt loop, which boils water to drive a turbine and generator.

buildSteps.title: Shut down safely
buildSteps.detail: If temperature rises too high, the freeze valve melts and the fuel salt drains by gravity into a subcritical tank where fission stops.

prerequisites.why: the Molten-Salt Reactor Experiment in the 1960s proved the concept, but long-term alloy and graphite performance remains challenging.
breeding uranium-233 from thorium has been demonstrated in test reactors, but continuous, large-scale reprocessing of hot fluoride salt is unproven.
tritium permeates through hot metal and must be captured to prevent release and to meet safety limits.
neutron irradiation damages graphite, so a power plant needs replaceable or improved moderator blocks.
existing nuclear regulations assume solid fuel pins, not a circulating molten fuel that is also the coolant.

pathway.milestone: small experimental reactors studying salt chemistry and materials
pathway.unlocks: data on corrosion, fission product behaviour, and safe operation.

pathway.milestone: pilot reactors of a few tens of megawatts that demonstrate thorium breeding and online reprocessing
pathway.unlocks: proof that the fuel cycle can be closed.

pathway.milestone: prototype power plants of 100–300 megawatts connected to the grid
pathway.unlocks: reliability and economic data for commercial design.

pathway.milestone: commercial thorium molten-salt fleets with closed fuel cycles
pathway.unlocks: abundant-fuel baseload power with passive safety.
